question: Do independently deposited binders (different PDB entries) of the same disordered-epitope peptide report the same backbone conformation (conformer-selection signal) or distinct ones (induced-fit signal)?

universe.sweep_rule: peptide-like antigen chains (<=40 residues) become expansion components; protein-embedded matches recorded as context only

metric: C-alpha RMSD after Kabsch superposition restricted to overlapped residues; identical peptides use full length; >=4 usable CA points

tiers.grounding: T2.1 v2 moderate-perturbation tier 1.5-3.0 A (frozen, read-only reference); thresholds fixed before any pair RMSD was computed

floor_control.rule: same-entry same-binder (NCS-copy) pairs expected mean <= 0.5 A
floor_control.invalidation: mean > 1.0 A -> floor_check_failed; all same-entry diversity interpretations downgraded

dihedral_windows.purpose: descriptive class per bound copy; no mechanism claim

validity_gates: peptide chain located by exact substring, never a binder chain
overlap >= 5 residues for distinct windows; full length for identical peptides
multiple candidate chains are recorded, never silently dropped

family_verdict_rules.conformer_sharing: all valid cross-entry pairs tier same_bound_conformer

stop_rules.starvation: 0 families with a valid cross-entry pair -> coordinate_starvation
stop_rules.generalization: <3 cross-entry families -> single_or_few_family_descriptive, insufficient for generalization

claims_boundary: Coordinate bookkeeping only; no model, no scores, no network. Verdicts describe deposited bound conformations; they do not establish conformer selection as a mechanism, binding, affinity, or any design claim. Read-only references: flex_j0 preregistration, T2.1 v2 tier, INTEGRATIVE_ANALYSIS section 2.2.
